title: Add minimal Kubernetes manifests + Dedicated/Private deployment notes (probes, shutdown, sizing)
author: Bruno Silva
body: Summary: This adds a minimal, copy/paste-friendly Kubernetes deployment path for the quickstart templates (rag + agents + combined) and documents the knobs we expect teams to adjust when targeting Redwood Dedicated / Private clusters. The manifests include readiness/liveness probes, graceful shutdown (preStop + terminationGracePeriodSeconds), resource requests/limits, basic Pod security context, and clear placeholders for secrets/config. Motivation: We keep seeing users go from local -> "throw it into k8s" and end up with (a) no health checks (bad rollout behavior), (b) requests getting cut off during node drains, (c) missing timeouts / env var mismatch between README and deployment, and (d) no guidance for Dedicated/Private network constraints. This PR provides a minimal baseline we can stand behind without becoming a full Helm chart. What’s included: (1) templates/k8s/base with Deployment, Service, ConfigMap (non-secret settings), and an optional Ingress example; (2) per-template overlays via Kustomize to set the container command, ports, and env defaults; (3) probe endpoints wired to the existing /healthz and /readyz routes in the FastAPI/Node services; (4) docs notes for Dedicated/Private: DNS + egress allow-listing, private control-plane endpoints, OTEL collector placement, and log/trace correlation headers. Key design decisions: - Kustomize over Helm for now (keeps “minimal” promise; easy to vendor into customer repos). - Secrets are NOT included as checked-in objects; we reference a Secret by name (REDWOOD_API_KEY, optional REDWOOD_ORG) and include a docs snippet showing `kubectl create secret generic ...` for local clusters. - Probes default to conservative timings to avoid noisy restarts on cold start or first model warmup; readiness is separate from liveness. - RollingUpdate is configured with maxUnavailable=0 to reduce downtime during activation. - Graceful shutdown: preStop sleeps 5s and we rely on the app’s SIGTERM handler to stop accepting new requests while finishing in-flight streaming responses (where possible). Dedicated/Private notes (in docs): - Dedicated: recommend pinning to a node pool with predictable egress and using PodDisruptionBudgets for higher-availability deployments; mention using Redwood routing policies and region pinning if the cluster is in a single region. - Private (VPC/on-prem): call out that clusters may have restricted outbound; document required outbound destinations (Redwood Private control plane / telemetry endpoints as applicable) and suggest placing an OpenTelemetry Collector in-cluster to buffer/export traces/metrics. - Suggest aligning correlation IDs: propagate `x-request-id` into logs, and pass through `traceparent` to the Redwood API so traces join in Console. - Mention using NetworkPolicy where required; keep sample policy in docs only (varies heavily by CNI). Validation: Applied to kind and GKE dev cluster; verified probes, graceful shutdown on rollout, and that the app emits OTEL traces/metrics when OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is set. This PR does not add HPA by default; we mention how to scale replicas and what to watch (p95 latency, 429s, timeouts) using the quickstart dashboards. Follow-ups: - If/when we standardize on a full chart, we can build from this base. - Separate PR will add a small “k8s smoke” job in CI once we settle on a cluster runner (tracked in ENG-2848).
commits: k8s: add base manifests (Deployment/Service/ConfigMap) with probes and securityContext
k8s: add kustomize overlays for rag/agents/combined templates
docs: add Dedicated/Private deployment notes + sizing and rollout guidance
runtime: ensure /readyz returns non-200 until app init completes (node + python)
chore: align env var names in manifests with template contract
checks: CI: lint (pass), unit (pass), template-smoke-local (pass), docs-build (pass). Initial run failed on docs-build due to broken relative link in docs/deployment/kubernetes.md; fixed in commit 3 and reran (pass).
conversation: Sean Gallagher (SRE) review: “Thanks for keeping this minimal. A couple nits: (1) liveness initialDelaySeconds=5 seems aggressive for cold starts on small nodes; we’ve seen Node containers take 15–25s to start depending on image pull. (2) please set terminationGracePeriodSeconds to at least 30s given streaming responses. (3) can we avoid preStop ‘sleep’ and instead rely on app to drain?” Bruno Silva (author): “Good call. I bumped liveness initialDelaySeconds to 20s and added failureThreshold=6 (periodSeconds=5) to reduce flapping. Set terminationGracePeriodSeconds=60s. Keeping preStop sleep=5s as a small buffer to let the Service stop routing before SIGTERM-handling finishes wiring; happy to drop if you’d prefer.” Sean: “Ok with preStop if documented; add a one-liner explaining why it exists.” Rafael Mendes (SRE) review: “Please add maxSurge=1 / maxUnavailable=0 explicitly (default varies but we should be explicit). Also consider a PodDisruptionBudget example in docs only.” Bruno: “Added rolling update params; added a PDB example snippet in kubernetes.md (docs-only, not shipped as manifest).” Logan Wright (Telemetry) review: “We should include OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES recommendations and keep cardinality safe. Also: if we want traces to join, mention passing traceparent header through to Redwood API.” Bruno: “Added docs section ‘Telemetry wiring’ with OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES (service.version, deployment.environment) and a note about not adding tenant_id as resource attr (log field only). Added explicit note about traceparent passthrough + x-request-id propagation.” Marcus Lin (Security) review: “Do not include Secret manifest examples that encourage committing secrets. If you include kubectl create secret commands, make sure docs emphasize non-prod vs prod (ExternalSecrets/SealedSecrets/etc). Also set runAsNonRoot and readOnlyRootFilesystem if feasible.” Bruno: “Removed Secret YAML example entirely; replaced with kubectl commands + ‘Production options’ section pointing to ExternalSecrets and cloud secret managers. Added runAsNonRoot=true, allowPrivilegeEscalation=false, dropped capabilities, readOnlyRootFilesystem=true. For Node template we needed /tmp write for some libs; mounted emptyDir at /tmp in the Deployment.” Kira Thompson (Dedicated/Private docs) review: “Dedicated/Private notes look good. Can we clarify what changes when the customer is running Redwood Private control plane inside the same cluster vs separate VPC?” Bruno: “Added a short ‘Private topology variants’ note: (a) app in customer cluster calling private endpoint; (b) app co-located with Private control plane. Included DNS/service discovery considerations and that OTEL export may stay in-cluster.” Approvals: Sean Gallagher approved after probe/graceful shutdown updates. Logan Wright approved after telemetry doc updates. Marcus Lin approved after secret handling changes. Kira Thompson approved after Dedicated/Private clarifications. Merge: Squash merged by Bruno Silva.
release_notes: Quickstarts now include minimal Kubernetes manifests (Kustomize-based) with readiness/liveness probes, resource defaults, and guidance for Dedicated/Private deployment constraints.
